chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who has days [of fasting] from the month of Ramadan [to make up], can he fast optional [fasts]? He said: No, until he makes up what is upon him from the month of Ramadan.
ai.seo_question: Can I fast voluntary fasts if I still have missed days from Ramadan?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the obligation of making up missed Ramadan fasts takes precedence over voluntary fasting, a ruling derived from the principle that the debt to Allah must be settled before seeking additional reward. This establishes a hierarchical structure in Shia jurisprudence where 'qada' (making up) is treated as a binding duty that suspends the permissibility of 'nafl' (voluntary) acts until fulfilled. The ruling underscores the seriousness of unfulfilled obligatory duties in the sight of the Imam.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl, from Abu Al Sabbah Al Kinany who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man upon whom are Fasts from a Month of Ramazan (to make up for), can he Fast optional ones?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, until he makes up for what is upon him from a Month of Ramazan’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ‘Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from abu al-Sabbah al-Kinaniy who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who owes several days of Qada’ (compensatory fast) for the fast of the month of Ramadan if he can fast optional fast. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, he cannot do so before completing Qada’ (compensatory fast) of what is due upon him of the month of Ramadan.’”
